From: Lucy Park <lucy.park@acmehealth.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: compliance-team@acmehealth.com
Date: Sat, 21 Jun 2025 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Residency scope covenant & private network proofs (Acme Health)

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the product walkthrough yesterday — the team appreciated the latency numbers and the Dedicated option. Before legal signs off, our compliance group asked for a short covenant confirming the following items so we can close the SOC/SIG tranche of our security review: 

1) A statement that production customer data for our account will be hosted only in Redwood-managed nodes within the US (no replication to EU/APAC unless explicitly configured by Acme Health).
2) Confirmation that Redwood Private (VPC) traffic will terminate on a customer-dedicated VPC endpoint and that operator access is via a documented keystore operator roster (no shared operator keys).
3) An exported control matrix or simple CSV listing where artifacts live (SOC 2 exhibits / CAIQ pointers / SIG answers that map to hosting controls).

Can you provide a short covenant and any evidence pack we can attach to the contract? If easier, we can accept a DocuSign acknowledgment.

Best,
Lucy
Lucy Park
Senior Information Security Manager
Acme Health

--
Acme Health | compliance-team@acmehealth.com
From: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
To: Lucy Park <lucy.park@acmehealth.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 23 Jun 2025 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency scope covenant & private network proofs (Acme Health)

Hi Lucy —

Thanks — looping in Irene (security & compliance) and Sean (customer ops) to assemble a concise packet. Short answers up front so you can share with legal: 

- Residency covenant: Redwood confirms that, for the Acme Health account as configured under deal DEAL-ACM-00321, customer production data will be hosted only in US-region Redwood-managed nodes and will not be replicated to EU/APAC unless Acme explicitly requests cross-region replication in writing. This is enforceable via account-level zone binding in our control plane and documented in the attached residency matrix.

- VPC/private networking: Redwood Private provides a customer-dedicated private endpoint (single-tenant peering) for Acme. Traffic to customer-owned VPCs terminates at that endpoint; operator access to the operator keystore is recorded and whitelisted per account. We do not share operator keystore credentials across tenants — see attached keystore operator roster (redacted).

- Artifacts: Attached CSV maps CAIQ/SIG items that reference hosting and network controls. We also included an annotated topology image showing where logs, keystores, and control-plane telemetry are retained.

Next steps: Irene, can you confirm the keystore/operator statement below and add any CAIQ pointers? Sean, can you set up a short DocuSign acknowledgment we can push to Lucy if Acme prefers a signature?

Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Head of Customer Compliance
Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: Lucy Park <lucy.park@acmehealth.com>, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2025 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency scope covenant & private network proofs (Acme Health)

Hi Lucy / Naomi,

I reviewed the account config and the artifacts Naomi referenced. A few clarifications for Acme's compliance packet: 

- Keystore/operator practice: We maintain a per-account operator roster (attached PDF). The operator roster includes the hashed operator key fingerprint and personnel list for all keystore access requests. For Private deployments we support HSM-backed key material; Redwood's day-2 operator processes require multi-person approval for key access and are logged in our audit trail (SOC 2 exhibit ref: SOC2-CR-AUD-2024).

- Control mappings: The attached CSV (redwood_residency_matrix_v1.csv) maps CAIQ hosting questions (e.g., CC-PHI-02: data location control) to our artifact IDs and public docs. Where a CAIQ answer references operational detail we included a pointer to the SOC 2 exhibit or internal runbook excerpt (read-only link included).

- Network topology: The PNG shows the peering boundary we enforce for Dedicated/Private accounts. For Acme specifically, the tenant will be restricted to the us-east-1 and us-west-2 nodes; we will not enroll it in any EU/APAC clusters without a written change request from Acme's security contact.

If you'd like, we can replace redacted personnel names in the operator roster with full names once we have an NDA amendment executed (standard for personnel disclosure).

Irene Choi
Senior Security Engineer, Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_residency_matrix_v1.csv; keystore_operator_roster_2025-06.pdf; privatenet-topology-annotated.png
From: Lucy Park <lucy.park@acmehealth.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: compliance-team@acmehealth.com, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 25 Jun 2025 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency scope covenant & private network proofs (Acme Health)

Naomi / Irene —

This looks good and aligns with what our legal/compliance team needs. Two quick asks before we attach to the contract: 

1) Can you provide a 1-paragraph covenant we can paste into an SOW addendum that mirrors the residency sentence above? Legal would like explicit wording they can sign.
2) For the keystore roster: can you confirm you will provide full operator names and phone numbers under our mutual NDA addendum? We will request that as an appendix for our security operations audit.

If you can send the covenant and the DocuSign packet, I can route this to contracting today. Thanks for the quick turnaround.

Regards,
Lucy
